name: cta
description: UIDS cta component contract, preserving the verified 4.x rendering and documenting the proposed Figma representation.

figma.note: BUILT (Phase 3), corrected 2026-08-17 against an independent reference build (UIDS – Generated Library, fileKey xGTjxedGs7F2Riq0PkglSa). Orientation (3) x Background (5) x ButtonAlignRight (2) = 3x5x2 = 30 variants, NOT the 25 an earlier draft proposed by collapsing orientation+button_align_right into a 5-value Layout axis. The set nests real Headline and Button instances rather than flattening to raw layers.
axisRationale: Three separate axes rather than a curated 5-value Layout axis: Orientation comes from Cta.vue's real '', 'left', 'inline' values, and Background from all five of its real background values (Background.props supports white even though the reference sample showed only four).

The nested Button's Color is BACKGROUND-DEPENDENT, not fixed: Secondary (black bg / white text) on the 6 Background=Gold variants, Primary (gold) on the other 24. Traced end to end through the production path — see knownIssues. Do not generalise this from a single sample: the flip is conditioned on the Background axis, so any sample that does not vary Background will read as uniformly one colour and be wrong.
The nested Headline is Level=H2 / Style=UPPERCASE (Antonio Bold, textCase UPPER), not Style=Default (Roboto Medium) — verified against the actual font on both variants.
headline_style is NOT a CTA-owned axis: a designer wanting a different title treatment swaps the nested Headline instance's own Style property.
deliberateOmissions: button_label absence (a button-less CTA) gets no variant of its own — a labelled documentation frame showing the Button instance deleted, rather than an axis that multiplies the set.
figma.precedent: Brand Bar -> Logo / Form Fieldset -> Form Item (nested instances).

options.name: headline_style
options.description: Title style, passed straight through to the nested Headline instance's `text_style` prop (Cta.vue:75). Cta.vue declares `type: String, default: ''` with NO validator enforcing these three values — the Storybook control (Cta.stories.js:20-34) restricts to ['uppercase','serif',''] with labels 'Antonio (default)'/'Zilla Slab'/'Roboto'. Same no-validator looseness class as Headline's own text_style (contracts/headline.json) and Inline's size/alignment props.

code.notes: Maps 1:1 onto the child's real option (see contractSketch.children) — the NAME differs (headline_style vs Headline's own text_style) even though the values/default are identical. CTA does not restyle title text itself; all treatment tokens live in contracts/headline.json, not here.

figma.notes: Deliberately NOT a CTA-owned axis (confirms the survey's judgment call, for an updated reason — see contractSketch.behavior's CORRECTION entry: Headline now HAS its own Style/Level axes, having shipped in Phase 2, so this is a `children`-modeled pass-through rather than a deferred unknown). If CTA's Figma set nests a real Headline instance (recommended, see figmaProposal.collapseNotes), a designer swaps THAT instance's own Style property directly; CTA's set does not duplicate it.

options.name: url
options.description: href, passed straight through to the nested Button instance's `url` prop (Cta.vue:85). Cta.vue declares `url: { type: String }` with NO default key at all (true Vue-level default is `undefined`, not '') — passing an explicit `undefined` through causes Vue to fall back to Button's OWN prop default (''), so the practically-rendered result still matches ''. Inherits Button's own url a11y caveat unchanged (an empty href stays focusable and navigates to the current page, contracts/button.json a11y).

code.notes: No explicit default in Cta.vue's own source (contrast button_icon/orientation/button_align_right/background, which do declare one) — see description.

figma.notes: Not a variant axis (content/link property), consistent with Button's own url option.

options.name: details
options.description: Body copy. ALSO doubles as the gate for whether `.cta__content` renders at all (`v-if="details"`, Cta.vue:80) and as the `details` slot's own fallback content (`<slot name="details">{{ details }}</slot>`, Cta.vue:81). Cta.vue declares `details: { type: String }` with no default key (true default `undefined`, falsy either way for the v-if). See contractSketch.knownIssues for the resulting slot/prop gating inconsistency versus `title` and `button_label`.

code.notes: Unlike `title` (gated on real slot presence, `$slots.title`) and `button_label` (gated on the prop consistently for BOTH the wrapper and its own slot fallback), `details` gates the wrapper on the PROP only, while ALSO being the slot's fallback — see knownIssues.

options.name: orientation
options.description: Layout mode. '' = centered (no modifier class — the base .cta rules ARE the centered layout); left = adds cta--left; inline = adds cta--inline. No Vue validator restricts the value (`orientation: { type: String, default: '' }`) — `className(props.orientation)` (Cta.vue:57) emits `cta--{anything}` for an arbitrary string, but only these three have matching SCSS. Combines orthogonally with button_align_right at the code level — see contractSketch.behavior for the resulting cascade interaction when both are set.

code.notes: '' emits no modifier class at all.

figma.notes: CORRECTED from a shared collapsed 'Layout' axis to its own real axis, matching the reference build's naive full cross (see identity.figma.note).

options.name: button_align_right
options.description: Right-aligns the button and switches justify-content/text-align to left on the root, plus md-breakpoint flex-basis rules on .cta__content/.cta__link and a `:not([class*="cta--left"])`-guarded text-align:center override on .cta__container. See contractSketch.behavior for exactly how this interacts with orientation='left' at the CSS cascade level (the :not() guard does not fully separate the two states).

code.notes: Applied via a `['button_align_right'].forEach(...)` single-item loop (Cta.vue:50-54) — functionally identical to a plain `if`, see claims (redundant construct, not a behavior bug).

figma.notes: CORRECTED from a shared collapsed 'Layout' axis to its own real axis, matching the reference build's naive full cross (see identity.figma.note).

options.name: button_label
options.description: Button text. ABSENCE IS SIGNIFICANT (Button default-slot precedent, contracts/button.json) but STRONGER: when falsy, the ENTIRE `<footer class="cta__link">` wrapper — and therefore the whole nested Button instance — does not render at all (`v-if="button_label"`, Cta.vue:84). This differs from Button's own no-text state (`.bttn--no-text`), which still renders an (inaccessible) button element; a button-less CTA renders no button whatsoever. Cta.vue declares no default key.

code.notes: Also the fallback content for the `button_label` slot — the wrapper v-if and the slot fallback consistently share this one prop (contrast `details`, see knownIssues).

figma.notes: Not modeled as an axis (confirms the survey's judgment call) — a button-less CTA is a page-author content variation, not a CTA-owned visual axis. See openQuestions.

options.name: button_icon
options.description: Icon markup passed into the nested Button instance's `icon` slot. Only ever reachable when button_label is ALSO truthy, since both sit inside the same `v-if="button_label"` footer (Cta.vue:84-89) — button_icon has no independent gating of its own.

figma.notes: Instance-swap/content property on the nested Button instance, not a CTA-owned axis.

options.name: background
options.description: Background color of the root element, via the shared `background` foundation (contracts/background.json, shipped Phase 2 — see the CORRECTION in contractSketch.behavior). Spread `...Background.props` into Cta.vue's defineProps (Cta.vue:41), applied by `Background.addBackgroundClass` (Cta.vue:48). CTA is a COLOR-ONLY consumer of the foundation (shared/background.ts's plain `props`/`colors` shape, NOT the pattern-capable `allBackgroundProps`) — no pattern option is exposed, matching Callout's own identical restriction (phase3-specs/callout.json).

code.notes: Class is added by Background.addBackgroundClass, not by CTA's own class-computation logic — the same shared-module pattern as Button's borderless (contracts/button.json) and Callout's identical background option (phase3-specs/callout.json).

figma.notes: CORRECTED axis name from 'Color' to 'Background', matching the built set and the reference build's own prop naming. Binds the EXISTING background foundation's color/bg/* variables (contracts/background.json), which CTA's own tokensUsed does NOT claim (one-contract-per-token, Phase 2 scoping rule) — those are Semantic-tier bindings, which check-figma's bound-var rule always allows regardless of contract ownership. THIS AXIS ALSO DRIVES THE NESTED BUTTON'S COLOUR: the Gold value flips the Button instance to Color=Secondary (black bg / white text), every other value leaves it Primary (gold) — see knownIssues for the verified production chain. A designer changing this axis on an instance gets that flip automatically because each variant carries its own Button instance.

slots.name: title
slots.description: The CTA's headline content, wrapped in a nested Headline instance (see contractSketch.children).
slots.behavior: ABSENCE IS SIGNIFICANT (Button default-slot precedent): the whole `.cta__title` wrapper — and the nested Headline instance inside it — only renders when the REAL slot is present (`v-if="$slots.title"`, Cta.vue:74). This checks slot presence, not any prop; there is no `title` prop on Cta.vue at all (see claims/knownIssues re: Cta.stories.js's stray `:title` binding).

figma.notes: Modelled as a nested Headline instance, not a bare text layer, so its own Style/Level stay Headline's concern — see figmaProposal.collapseNotes.

slots.name: details
slots.description: Body copy; falls back to the `details` prop when no slot content is given.
slots.behavior: Gated on the `details` PROP (`v-if="details"`, Cta.vue:80), NOT on slot presence — see contractSketch.knownIssues for the resulting inconsistency (slot content alone, with no `details` prop set, silently renders nothing).

slots.name: button_label
slots.description: The nested Button instance's label content; falls back to the `button_label` prop.
slots.behavior: Gated on the `button_label` PROP, consistently, for both the wrapper (`v-if`, Cta.vue:84) and the slot's own fallback content (Cta.vue:86) — self-consistent, contrast `details`.

figma.notes: Bound to the nested Button instance's Label property.

slots.name: button_icon
slots.description: The nested Button instance's icon slot content; no fallback of its own.
slots.behavior: Only reachable when button_label is also truthy (same v-if scope, Cta.vue:84-89) — see the button_icon option.

figma.notes: Bound to the nested Button instance's Icon boolean/slot.

fixed.color: primary — EXCEPT background=gold, where it is secondary. Not a CTA prop: Cta.vue passes no colour at all (buttonClasses returns ['']), so `primary` is Button's own default; the gold-background flip comes from the downstream uids_base override, not from UIDS. See knownIssues for the verified chain and the 2026-08-17 ruling.

behavior: CORRECTION to phase3-inputs/cta.json's central premise: crossComponentDeps says 'Headline is NOT yet migrated (no contract/tokens/Figma set)' — FALSE. contracts/headline.json, tokens/components/headline.json and a 30-variant Figma set (componentSetId 168:75) all shipped in Phase 2 (commit 0d4d19f213, 2026-08-15). Its recommendation to keep headline_style out of CTA's Figma axes is STILL correct, for a different reason: Headline has its own Style/Level axes, so headline_style is modeled here as a `children` relationship to contracts/headline.json (see contractSketch.children), not a deferred unknown. Its 'background contract question... architect needs to decide whether background becomes its own foundation contract now' is ALSO stale: contracts/background.json shipped in the SAME batch, so CTA's background option delegates to it as an existing foundation (see openQuestions #2).

CTA nests two already-migrated components rather than owning visual identity itself: Headline (title, contracts/headline.json) and Button (link, contracts/button.json) — see contractSketch.children for exactly which of each child's options CTA exposes (pass-through) versus fixes (explicitly or by omission).

CTA also consumes the `background` foundation (contracts/background.json) without claiming its tokens, and its own container padding partially overlaps the `layout` foundation's already-tokenized gutter value ($mobile-width-gutter IS layout/gutter/width/mobile, tokens/semantic/layout.json) — see geometryNotTokenized. One contract claims each token (Phase 2 scoping rule); CTA's own tokensUsed stays limited to cta/gap.

orientation and button_align_right combine orthogonally in code (independent classes, no mutual exclusion in Cta.vue), but the CSS cascade resolves ties by SOURCE ORDER, not by any explicit precedence. When BOTH cta--left and cta--button-align-right are present (orientation='left' + button_align_right=true): `.cta--left`'s `justify-content: unset` (cta.scss:64, declared AFTER .cta--button-align-right's block) wins over `.cta--button-align-right`'s `justify-content: left` (cta.scss:30) — both are single-class selectors of equal specificity, so the later declaration governs. `text-align: left` is identical in both rules, so it never conflicts. A real, reachable, Figma-represented state ('Left + Button Right', see figmaProposal); the proposed LeftButtonRight story (storyAudit) pins the net visual result. What survives the tie: behavior[5].

The `orientation='inline'` + `button_align_right=true` combination is ALSO reachable in code (both are independent classes) but is deliberately excluded from the Figma Layout axis (5 curated values, not the naive 3x2=6 cross) and from the proposed new stories, matching Button's own transparent+light_font 'code-only combination' precedent (contracts/button.json). Its actual cascade outcome (a three-way conflict across .cta--button-align-right, .cta--inline, and their un-guarded overlapping selectors on .cta__link/.cta__content) was not fully traced here — flagged in openQuestions rather than exhaustively specified, to avoid over-scoping a combination nothing currently exercises or plans to represent.

WHAT SURVIVES THE TIE in behavior[3]: all of `.cta--button-align-right`'s OTHER rules (md flex-wrap:nowrap, `.cta__title` flex-basis:100%, `.cta__content`/`.cta__link` flex 0 1 48% at md, `.cta__link` justify-content:end/align-self:baseline) still apply in the combined state — only the root's `justify-content` is overridden.
changes: 2026-08-24 — A CTA IS ALWAYS NARROW. The design system owner's ruling from a generated-page review: a CTA's text must never run the full page width. This is a DECISION, not a fidelity correction: `max-width` does not occur anywhere in src/scss/components/cta.scss (zero occurrences, verified 2026-08-24), so a CTA in a full-width container spans it, and that is what 4.x ships. Nothing about the rendering changes — no token moves, no class added, no pixel shifts in any story — so this entry moves no pixels and the contract version does not move with it, exactly as badge.json changes[2] established for a public-shape decision. What changes is that a full-width CTA is now WRONG rather than merely unconstrained. How the constraint is carried instead: changes[1].

2026-08-24, continues changes[0] — THE NARROW CONSTRAINT IS CARRIED BY COMPOSITION, NOT CSS: the section supplies the full-bleed band (section.layout__container.bg--gold), a div.page__container--narrow inside it caps the measure, and the CTA itself takes background="" so it does not paint a second band inside the first. Published to agents as contracts/rules.json cta-is-always-narrow. Recorded rather than left as silence because a later agent reading cta.scss will find no width rule and reasonably conclude the absence is an oversight to fix in CSS — it is not; if the constraint is ever moved into cta.scss that is a real rendering change needing its own contract-first pass and a fresh ruling.
knownIssues: cta_uids3.scss (src/scss/components/cta_uids3.scss, 122 lines) targets an entirely different, older markup shape (.cta__wrapper, .element--left, .bold-headline/.headline) that Cta.vue never renders, and is unreferenced by THIS repo's src/scss/uids.scss (only 'components/cta' i.e. cta.scss is @use'd, uids.scss:14). It is, however, NOT dead in production — see claims for the full verified chain (a byte-identical vendored copy, a separate downstream uids_base wrapper that @uses it, and a matching compiled Drupal library). Do not propose deletion; out of scope for this contract. The eventual contracts/cta.json should list src/scss/components/cta_uids3.scss under identity.relatedPaths and the uids_base wrapper + vendored path + library key under identity.downstreamPaths, mirroring how contracts/headline.json already lists the SAME downstream file for its own unrelated .bold-headline coupling.

Cta.vue imports Borderless (src/components/shared/borderless.ts) but never spreads its props or calls addBorderlessClass — a dead import (see claims). Drop it during the SCSS-consumes-tokens step; CTA has no borderless option today.

Cta.vue's buttonClasses computed (lines 63-67) always returns [''] regardless of props and contributes no class to the rendered `<uids-button>` — dead code (see claims). Drop or repurpose during migration; today it is pure noise on the button element.

Cta.stories.js's Template renders `<div :class="getClasses" ...>` inside the `#title` slot, but `getClasses` is never defined anywhere in the file (see claims) — likely a copy-paste leftover. The SAME template also binds `:title="args.title"` on `<uids-cta>` even though Cta.vue declares no `title` prop; since Cta.vue never sets `inheritAttrs: false`, it becomes a plain HTML `title`-attribute fallthrough onto the root `<div>` (Cta.vue:72) — a browser tooltip, not component behavior. The story only works because the REAL title mechanism (the `#title` named slot, gated by `v-if="$slots.title"`) is ALSO wired next to it (Cta.stories.js:96). The `title` argType (Cta.stories.js:53-55, `control: {type:'text'}`) matches no real Cta.vue prop — a stale arg, Headline size/url/class precedent (see storyAudit.staleArgs). Clean up both when the story is next touched for the new baseline stories.

The `details` slot's wrapper is gated on the `details` PROP (`v-if="details"`, Cta.vue:80), not on slot presence — a consumer supplying ONLY `<template #details>` markup with no `details` prop gets nothing rendered; the slot content is silently dropped. Inconsistent with `title` (gated on real `$slots.title` presence) and with `button_label` (gated on the prop for BOTH the wrapper and its own slot fallback, so at least internally self-consistent). Recommend a public-shape ruling (switch to `$slots.details`, or document as-shipped) rather than silently 'fixing' it during migration — see openQuestions.

orientation has no Vue prop validator (`type: String, default: ''`) — any string reaches `className()` and becomes `cta--{value}` (Cta.vue:57), but only '', 'left', 'inline' have matching SCSS. Same looseness class as Inline's size/alignment props (contracts/inline.json) and Button's color accepting the dead 'link' value (contracts/button.json). As-shipped; not tightened here — see openQuestions.

url, details, and button_label are declared with `type: String` and NO default key in Cta.vue (contrast button_icon/orientation/button_align_right/background, which do declare explicit defaults) — their real Vue-level default is `undefined`, not ''. This only has a practical effect for `url` (undefined passes through to Button's own url prop, which then supplies its own '' default) — details/button_label already branch on truthiness for their v-if gates regardless of whether the value is '' or undefined.

UIDS IN ISOLATION renders the CTA button gold on a gold background, and that IS a real contrast bug in this repo: buttonClasses (Cta.vue:63) returns [''], so uids-button falls through to its `primary` default and computes rgb(255,205,0) in every context — verified live in Storybook against bg--black, bg--gold, bg--gray and default; it never flips. NO REAL PAGE RENDERS THAT STATE, because the downstream platform patches it: knownIssues[8] has the verified chain, knownIssues[9] the ruling. OWNER: uiowa#5149, pulling the override upstream into UIDS's own cta.scss — deliberately NOT done here, since that is a real code change during a migration needing its own design decision and regression baselines.

THE DOWNSTREAM PATCH THAT HIDES knownIssues[7], verified as a production chain 2026-08-17: (1) uids_base/templates/uids/cta.html.twig:30 always emits `bttn bttn--primary`, so the gold default is genuinely what the markup asks for; (2) uids_base/scss/components/cta.scss:63 overrides it for gold backgrounds only — `[class*="bg--gold"] .cta__link .bttn--primary { background: $secondary; color: #fff }`, plus `i, svg { color: $primary }`; (3) that rule ships — it is present in the compiled asset uids_base/assets/css/components/cta.css, which uids_base.libraries.yml:205 attaches as the `cta` library. The override sits under a `// @todo remove once https://github.com/uiowa/uiowa/issues/5149 is completed` comment, so SiteNow itself treats it as a temporary downstream patch for this UIDS gap, not as intended platform-specific styling.

THE OVERRIDE IN knownIssues[8] IS A SECONDARY BUTTON, EXACTLY: its three channels are BYTE-IDENTICAL to UIDS's own Secondary button tokens — background var(--brand-secondary) = --uiowa-button-secondary-background; color #fff = --uiowa-button-secondary-color; icon var(--brand-primary) = --uiowa-button-secondary-icon-color. RULED 2026-08-17 (the design system owner, reversing the 2026-08-16 as-shipped ruling after reviewing the rendered set): the Figma set represents the PRODUCTION rendering — the 6 Background=Gold variants use Button Color=Secondary, the other 24 stay Primary. This changes no code; UIDS's own SCSS is untouched and still renders gold-on-gold in Storybook.

geometryNotTokenized.container-padding: `.cta { padding: $xlg $mobile-width-gutter; }` (cta.scss:6), constant at every breakpoint — no responsive override in the live file (contrast the dead-for-this-repo cta_uids3.scss, which DID switch to `$lg $desktop-width-gutter` at md). $xlg (2.5rem) has no existing primitive (tokens/primitives/spacing.json has no 2.5rem/250 step) and is shared Sass vocabulary across brand-footer.scss, blockquote.scss and cta.scss — tracked in sharedPrimitiveUsage for the deferred $xsm...$xxxlg sweep, not a CTA-owned value. Precedents: container-padding-precedents. Gutter half: container-padding-gutter-half.
geometryNotTokenized.align-right-layout-ratios: `flex: 0 1 48%` on .cta__content/.cta__link at md (cta.scss:40-45) and `flex-basis: 100%` on .cta__title (cta.scss:36-38), both only under .cta--button-align-right — breakpoint-gated layout ratios, not owned scale values, same class as Brand Bar's tab-overhang and Inline's own size-ratio geometry ('ratios are patterns, not tokens', contracts/inline.json).
geometryNotTokenized.inline-layout-ratios: `flex-basis: 30%` on .cta__link and the nested .cta__title at md, `flex: 1` on the nested .cta__content at md (cta.scss:75-94), all only under .cta--inline — same 'pattern, not token' treatment as align-right-layout-ratios.
geometryNotTokenized.link-alignment-mechanics: `.cta__link { justify-content: end; align-self: baseline; display: flex; }` (cta.scss:47-51, under .cta--button-align-right, NOT breakpoint-gated) — layout keywords with no numeric magnitude to tokenize.
geometryNotTokenized.container-padding-precedents: TWO INDEPENDENT PRECEDENTS support leaving $xlg exactly as it is rather than tokenizing pending a new primitive: (1) contracts/brand-footer.json (already migrated) uses the SAME $xlg for its own footer-padding and documents it as raw geometry, no primitive minted (contracts/brand-footer.json:141); (2) the sibling phase3-specs/blockquote.json, drafted the same session and independently, reaches the identical conclusion for blockquote's own $xlg use (center-orientation padding-top) — 'not yet an individually-mapped space.* primitive... tracked... for the deferred sweep'. This spec follows both.
geometryNotTokenized.container-padding-gutter-half: The $mobile-width-gutter half of the same padding declaration is NOT in the same boat: it already equals the layout foundation's `layout/gutter/width/mobile` token (tokens/semantic/layout.json, emits as `var(--uiowa-layout-gutter-width-mobile)`, confirmed in src/scss/abstracts/_tokens-generated.scss:106) — so if this padding is ever split or tokenized, only the $xlg half is actually blocked on a new primitive.
